extraction_metadata.document_summary: The Housing Price Prediction Model project is in the development stage, utilizing supervised machine learning models like Linear Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost. It is managed by Eljo Example, with Jordan Lee as the primary contact, and reviewed by Moe Example, within the Economic Analysis Division. The models are trained from scratch using internal historical housing market data, some of which contains personal information. The project explicitly states it does not use generative AI, LLMs, AI agents, information retrieval, fine-tuning, third-party models, external pretrained models, or foundation models. It uses open-source Python libraries. The system produces numeric price predictions and does not generate free-text. It is planned for internal operational deployment, requires human oversight, and is not externally facing or interacting with external end-users. The project is reviewing potential re-identification risks with model outputs and assessing whether housing variables may proxy for protected characteristics.
